text:
Elaine Park: Quick sync — we need a compact launch-gate note that answers: which SLOs are public, what we commit for Dedicated, how burst billing appears on invoices, and the minimal support/runbook deliverables. Can owners confirm items and blockers? :mag:

Raj Patel: Ack. I'll draft public SLOs and a short clause for Dedicated. Current canary numbers: p95 ~100ms, p99 ~245ms on standard hosts. Proposing public hosted SLOs below.

Raj Patel: Compact public SLO proposal (copyable):
```
service: redwood-inference-hosted
slo:
  latency_p50: 40ms
  latency_p95: 110ms
  latency_p99: 260ms
  availability: 99.9% monthly
  error_rate: <=0.5% monthly
```
Raj Patel: Note — we should not publish Dedicated numbers. Instead say: "Dedicated/Private customers receive contract-specific SLOs."

Sam O'Neill: Billing/FinOps notes: critical to show burst lines clearly. Proposal: two-tier invoice lines — Reserved Capacity (subscription) and On-Demand Burst (per-token). Example invoice snippet: `Reserved capacity — monthly commit $X; Burst usage — on-demand tokens Y @ $Z/token`. Also recommend we include a mini-reconciliation example for CS.

Sam O'Neill: Also: automated internal retries should never consume customer free credits. Bill only tokens on successful responses. Need engineering confirmation.

Tomas Vega: Monitoring/alert plan: I'll add two synthetics and a "burst-observed-usage" metric. Synthetics: short-probe (12 tokens /30s), streaming-probe (3k tokens /5m). Draft pages:
- page if availability < 99% over 5m
- page if p99 > 320ms for 15m
- page if error_rate > 0.75% for 10m
- ticket if synth failure rate > 5% over 30m

Tomas Vega: I'll link the dashboard to the runbook and put synthetic IDs in the doc.

Maria Lopez: Support/runbook: L1 checklist and triage steps done. Missing:
- explicit escalation routing for nights/weekends (SRE contact matrix)
- sample transcripts (4) with redaction guidance for training
- refund/billing dispute flow + owner for follow-up
I can finish transcripts and billing playbook if FinOps confirms invoice example.

Nina Chen: Legal: SLA language must avoid operational promises about fallbacks. Suggest wording: "Automated fallback policies may be used to preserve availability; such measures are operational mitigations and not separate SLA guarantees." Also need a short, non-technical credit sentence.

Nina Chen: Draft credit sentence: "If the monthly availability SLO is missed, eligible customers may receive a pro-rated service credit in accordance with the SLA."

Raj Patel: Engineering action items / edge behaviors:
- add x-model-fallback header when routing to lower-latency/quantized variant
- KV cache warm path for pinned models to avoid cold-start p99 spikes
- ensure billing-visible header for requests routed to Dedicated vs Hosted so usage attribution is accurate

deploy-bot: Canary deploy 2026-04-01T02:11Z -> success. Canary traffic 5% for 1h. Observed: p95=102ms, p99=246ms, errors=0.11%.

finance-bot: Billing simulation complete for sample tenant: reserved_commit=100k tokens/month, burst_used=12k tokens -> predicted burst charge $XYZ. CSV exported to /finance/simulations/launch-burst-2026-03.csv

Sam O'Neill: Two policy asks for docs:
- Public page should include a simple "what counts as burst" FAQ (e.g., exceeding reserved QPS or concurrent streams)
- Example invoice screenshot + mapping from UI to invoice lines

Raj Patel: Concurrency and quotas — engineering to prescribe default per-key QPS and concurrent stream caps. Suggest defaults: 120 QPS per API key, 10 concurrent streams per tenant for hosted. We can make them configurable for Dedicated.

Elaine Park: Docs owner decision: Publish one public SLO set for Hosted and a page explaining Dedicated contractual SLOs + contact flow. Maria to draft runbook snippets and the docs landing page; Raj to paste final SLO YAML; Sam to add invoice + FAQ; Tomas to add dashboard links; Nina to sign off on SLA sentence. Owners/dates?

Maria Lopez: I can deliver runbook snippets + 4 transcripts by Fri EOD. Will need finance invoice example.

Raj Patel: Final SLO YAML and header text by Tue. Also will add automatic-fallback header spec and the model-tagging for billing.

Sam O'Neill: I'll post invoice screenshot + FAQ draft by next Wed. I'll also add the reconciliation example for CS.

Tomas Vega: Dashboards and synthetic IDs by Thu. I'll wire alerts to the product pager and add rollback alert: auto-rollback if error-rate > 1% sustained for 10m.

Nina Chen: I'll confirm SLA credit sentence after SLOs locked. Will prepare a short legal-approved escalation email template for the runbook.

Raj Patel: Also recommend we include a short customer-facing matrix: "expected latency ranges by request shape" (small, medium, long-stream). That helps set expectations and reduces support volume.

Elaine Park: Decision checkpoint: if all owners hit dates above, PM will package this as the launch readiness artifact and route to Legal/Commercial. If blockers remain after owners' deadlines, escalate to the shipping committee.

Maria Lopez: noted. Will update the sprint sheet with dates and owners.

Elaine Park: Thanks everyone. If no other blockers, consider this the canonical thread for negotiating SLO publication policy vs billing transparency for GA. :white_check_mark:
